source_title: Delhi-NCR gets taste of winter after overnight rain, more showers in forecast - India Today
source_excerpt:
The Indian Meteorological Department has forecast light to moderate rain across Delhi-NCR on October 30, followed by partly cloudy skies on October 31. Conditions are expected to improve from November 1, while heavy rainfall alerts remain in place across several states.
Dark clouds and mist covered Delhi on Friday morning after overnight rainfall brought a noticeable chill to the national capital. The city recorded its wettest October day in four years, with the showers also pushing its monthly rainfall total to the highest level since 2022, news agency Press Trust of India (PTI) reported. Delhi received 61.4 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Friday, taking the cumulative rainfall for October to 123.3 mm, according to weather data cited by PTI. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The last time the national capital recorded higher rainfall on a single October day was on October 9, 2022, when it received 74 mm. Delhi recorded 128 mm of rainfall during the entire month that year. The rainfall also brought relief from pollution, improving Delhi's air quality to the 'satisfactory' category.
Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert for the next few hours, warning of more rain and thunderstorms across several parts of the capital. (Credits: PTI) IMD ISSUES RED ALERT, WARNS OF MORE RAIN The IMD said light to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning was very likely at most places across Delhi over the next three hours. Heavy rainfall was also expected at isolated locations.
The IMD said light to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning was very likely at most places across Delhi over the next three hours. Heavy rainfall was also expected at isolated locations.
The red alert covered southeast, east, central, northeast, south, southwest, west, northwest and north Delhi, along with Shahdara and New Delhi.
According to the IMD, the minimum temperature at Safdarjung, Delhi's base weather station, stood at 17.2 degrees Celsius, 1.1 degrees above normal. The maximum temperature was expected to settle around 27 degrees Celsius. The streets of Delhi got waterlogged. (Credits: PTI)
Palam recorded a minimum temperature of 15.4 degrees Celsius, 1.6 degrees below normal, while the Ridge registered 16.8 degrees Celsius, 0.5 degrees below normal. Lodi Road recorded 18 degrees Celsius, 3 degrees above normal, and Ayanagar registered 17.4 degrees Celsius, 1.1 degrees above normal.
Weather activity is expected to continue across the region before conditions gradually improve at the beginning of November. On October 29, Delhi experienced its coldest October day in four years with temperatures dropping 5.6°C below normal due to the weakening Cyclone Arnab. JHARODA KALAN RECORDS HIGHEST RAINFALL
Rainfall data for the period between 8.30 am on Thursday and 6 am on Friday showed that Jharoda Kalan received the highest rainfall at 89 mm.
Lodi Road recorded 63 mm, followed by Safdarjung at 56.5 mm. Jhajjar received 47 mm, while Narayana recorded 44.5 mm.
Pitampura received 42.5 mm of rainfall, Pusa recorded 41.5 mm and Kamla Nehru Nagar in Ghaziabad registered 41 mm. Pragati Maidan received 40.9 mm, while Gurugram recorded 36 mm.
Other locations that witnessed rainfall included Janakpuri (35.5 mm), Muradnagar (35 mm) and Northcap University in Gurugram (30 mm).
Lower rainfall totals were recorded in Mayur Vihar at 9 mm and Jafarpur at 1 mm. Data was unavailable for Najafgarh, Mehrauli, Chhatarpur and Hindon in Ghaziabad. advertisement DELHI AQI IMPROVES TO SATISFACTORY CATEGORY The overnight rainfall also improved Delhi's air quality, bringing the Air Quality Index (AQI) down to 90 at 9.30 am on Friday, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data cited by PTI. Data from the CPCB's SAMEER app showed that 36 monitoring stations across the capital recorded satisfactory air quality, while 16 stations remained in the moderate category. Under the CPCB's air quality classification, AQI readings between zero and 50 fall in the good category, while readings between 51 and 100 are classified as satisfactory. The moderate category covers readings between 101 and 200, followed by poor (201-300), very poor (301-400) and severe (401-500). The improvement came after Delhi's AQI had remained above 200 earlier in the week, placing it in the poor category. With 123.3 mm of rainfall already recorded this month and more showers forecast, Delhi's October rainfall total is nearing the 128 mm recorded in October 2022. The IMD's red alert indicates that rain and thunderstorms are likely to continue across parts of the capital over the next few hours. - Ends With PTI inputs
